title: Initial population growth ticks are daily, spread over about 15 days
rule: The fixed-value first phase of population growth runs on daily ticks, usually spread over 15 days: 13 full ticks plus partial ticks on days C+1 and C+15 (sometimes C+16). Frontier's Trailblazers Update 3 post says populations grow "on each weekly maintenance tick"; the guide's measured data says the early ticks are daily.
planner_implications: Model the first-phase growth per day, not per week. Before CRE Knowledge v0.3.0 this rule said "weekly"; that came from a DOCX extraction that lost the guide's footnote 27.
testing_status: Extracted from Mega Guide v2.3.0 measured data (CMDR Betel01); not live-verified in CRE
unknowns: Whether ticks after the first phase are daily or weekly

title: Population follows a hybrid curve
rule: Population uses fixed growth for the first 14 ticks and a logistic curve thereafter.
planner_implications: Short-run and long-run population planning should be modeled separately.

title: Output scales with the square root of population
rule: Commodity supply and demand scale with the square root of facility population.
planner_implications: Population gains have diminishing returns on production.

title: Stations reach about twenty percent of max population after 14 full ticks
rule: After roughly 15-16 days, a station reaches about 20% of max population and about 44.72% of max production.
planner_implications: Newly built stations become materially useful quickly even if they remain far from long-run maturity.

title: Full population maturation takes about a year
rule: A station takes about a year to approach its asymptotic population and production.
planner_implications: Long-run production planning differs materially from first-month bootstrapping.

title: Body and facility type both change asymptotic population
rule: Population tables vary by both body class and facility class, and many combinations have different K populations.
planner_implications: Do not reuse one facility's population profile across different bodies or tiers.

title: Tier 3 ELW orbitals reach about 3.1 billion asymptotic population
rule: The population table lists a Tier 3 orbital over an Earth-Like World at about 3.1 billion asymptotic population.
planner_implications: ELW T3 orbitals are population monsters and therefore major long-run output anchors.
unknowns: Whether all ELW orbital subclasses match that same ceiling

title: Tier 1 planetary ports can outclass Coriolis on population
rule: Tier 1 planetary ports at suitable bodies can exceed the population profile of a Tier 2 Coriolis in the guide's cited comparison cases.
planner_implications: Cheap ground ports can be valid population drivers rather than mere stepping stones, but body choice still matters heavily.

title: Population affects only its own facility output
rule: Population boosts the output of the facility it belongs to and does not automatically raise output across unrelated facilities in the same system.
planner_implications: Model facility-level output, not just system-total population.

title: Population affects emissions grade and BGS resistance
rule: Higher population appears to improve emissions grade and make BGS control harder to swing.
planner_implications: Population choices likely matter beyond commodity output alone, even if the exact magnitude is still loosely quantified.
unknowns: Exact magnitude of the emissions and BGS effects

title: Demolition may fail to reduce population
rule: The guide records anecdotal evidence that demolishing facilities may not reduce system population accordingly.
planner_implications: Demolition should not be recommended as a reliable population reset tactic yet.

title: The logistic phase inflects at 100 days for space ports and 120 for planetary ports
rule: The exact growth formula is published for space ports; the formula for ground ports appears similar, but its inflection point is 120 days instead of 100.
planner_implications: Planetary ports mature more slowly than space ports with the same asymptotic population.
